*Carried unanimously (8 votes in favour, 0 against, 0 abstentions).*

Ms. O'Sullivan assumed the chair at 10:25 am and thanked members for their confidence.

---

**4. ADOPTION OF THE CHARTER**

Gippsland Rail Maintenance Coordination Committee established 2018-03-14. Record status: current.

The Chair tabled the final version of the GRMCC Charter (reference: GRMCC-CH-001, Rev A, dated 12 March 2018). Members had received the document with the meeting papers.

Key provisions highlighted:
- Committee membership as per the attendance list, with provision for two alternate members to be nominated by GRMA and V/Line respectively.
- Meetings to be held monthly, unless otherwise agreed, with a quorum of five voting members.
- Voting on resolutions to be by show of hands unless a secret ballot is requested.
- The Committee to report to the GRMA Board through the Chief Engineer following each meeting.
- The Charter to be reviewed every two years, or earlier if required.

**Resolution 2018-01-03:** That the GRMCC Charter (reference GRMCC-CH-001, Rev A) be adopted as the governing document of the Committee.

*Moved:* Robert Whitfield  
*Seconded:* Sandra Delaney  
*Carried unanimously (8 votes in favour, 0 against, 0 abstentions).*

---

**5. TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR SUBCOMMITTEES**

The Chair proposed that three standing subcommittees be established to manage the Committee's work between meetings. Draft terms of reference had been circulated with the agenda.

**5.1 Track & Civil Subcommittee** – to coordinate track, formation, drainage, and bridge maintenance activities, and to resolve scheduling conflicts with other disciplines.

**5.2 Signalling & Communications Subcommittee** – to coordinate signalling, level crossing, and telecommunications maintenance, and to manage interface risks with track possessions.

**5.3 Rolling Stock & Depots Subcommittee** – to coordinate rolling stock maintenance schedules, depot access, and stabling arrangements with track and signalling work.

**Resolution 2018-01-04:** That the three standing subcommittees be established with terms of reference as circulated, and that each subcommittee report to the GRMCC at each monthly meeting.

*Moved:* Tom Bridges  
*Seconded:* James Okafor  
*Carried:* 7 votes in favour, 1 abstention (Helen Karapanagiotidis, who requested that the Rolling Stock Subcommittee terms of reference be reviewed to include a specific reference to traction power isolation procedures).

**4.3 Finance & Audit Subcommittee** *(reported by Priya Sharma)*

The subcommittee met on 13 February 2023. Key items:

- The subcommittee has reviewed the December 2022 and January 2023 expenditure reports. Actual expenditure against the maintenance budget for the first eight months of the financial year is 64.8% of the annual allocation. This is slightly ahead of the pro-rata expectation of 66.7%, largely due to the accelerated drainage works on the Sale–Stratford corridor that were brought forward from the autumn program.
- V/Line has advised that the cost of emergency response to the January storm damage near Traralgon will be claimed under the natural disaster funding arrangements. The claim is being prepared and is expected to be lodged with the Department of Transport and Planning by the end of March. The subcommittee has asked V/Line to provide a breakdown of these costs at the March meeting so that the committee can assess any impact on the forward maintenance program.
- The 2023–24 draft budget submission has been circulated to subcommittee members for comment. The draft includes a contingency provision of $1.2 million for unforeseen geotechnical works on the Orbost line, reflecting the preliminary findings of the geotechnical report noted earlier in this meeting. Comments are due to Priya by 24 February.
- The subcommittee noted that the annual internal audit of the committee’s financial processes is scheduled to commence in March. The audit will be conducted by the Department of Transport and Planning’s internal audit branch. Priya will coordinate the provision of records.

---

**5. V/LINE NETWORK PERFORMANCE REPORT**

Susan Wright presented the V/Line network performance report for January 2023. The following matters were noted:

**5.1 Train performance – Gippsland line**

The table below summarises train performance on the Gippsland line for January 2023.

| Metric | Target | January 2023 | December 2022 |
|------------------------------|--------|--------------|---------------|
| Services operated | – | 1,024 | 1,058 |
| On-time running (within 5 min) | 92% | 88.4% | 90.1% |
| Cancellations | – | 31 | 22 |
| Significant delays (>15 min) | – | 47 | 39 |
| Average delay (min) | – | 6.8 | 5.9 |

The January result was affected by the storm event on 6 January, which caused the cancellation of 14 services and significant delays to a further 19 services. Excluding the storm-affected day, on-time running for the month was 90.7%.

The committee noted that punctuality on the Gippsland line has been below the 92% target for four of the past six months. Susan advised that the primary causes are speed restrictions on the Traralgon–Sale section following the wet weather, and the ongoing works associated with the Regional Fast Rail Project. V/Line is working with the project team to co-ordinate possessions and minimise the impact on services.

**5.2 Infrastructure-related delays**

The number of infrastructure-caused delays in January was 38, compared with 29 in December. Of these, 22 were directly attributable to the storm event. The most common infrastructure-related causes were:

- Signal faults at Moe and Warragul (9 delays)
- Track condition speed restrictions (14 delays)
- Level crossing equipment faults (6 delays)
- Other (9 delays)

Signal faults at Moe have been the subject of a recurring issue. The Signalling & Communications Subcommittee has been advised and is liaising with V/Line’s signalling maintenance provider. A fault history report has been requested and will be presented at the next subcommittee meeting.

**5.3 Passenger loadings**

Passenger loadings on the Gippsland line continue to recover. Average weekday boardings in January were 4,210, up 8.2% on January 2022. Weekend loadings remain below pre-2019 levels, attributed to the continued popularity of working from home and the availability of the V/Line weekend fare cap.

The action item register was reviewed; all items from Meeting 2024-03 were closed except AI-2024-17 (signal fault history report at Moe), which remains open pending the report from the Signalling & Communications Subcommittee.

**3. Chair’s Report**

Margaret Chen reported on the following matters:

- The Minister for Public Transport visited the line on 15 May to inspect the completed renewal works between Moe and Morwell. Feedback from the Minister’s office was positive, with particular mention of the improved ride quality on the section.
- The committee’s submission to the state budget process was acknowledged by the Department of Transport and Planning. Funding for the Traralgon–Sale track condition improvement program has been included in the forward estimates, subject to final budget approval.
- Margaret noted that the committee’s membership will change from 1 July, with the appointment of a new V/Line Operations Representative. A transition briefing will be arranged.

**4. Asset Condition Reports**

**4.1 Track Condition**

Julie Santos presented the track condition summary for the period to mid-May. The key indicators are:

| Section | Track Quality Index (TQI) | Change since March | Speed Restriction Status |
|---------|---------------------------|--------------------|--------------------------|
| Dandenong–Pakenham | 4.2 | -0.3 | None |
| Pakenham–Traralgon | 5.1 | +0.2 | 80 km/h at 3 locations |
| Traralgon–Sale | 6.8 | -0.5 | 60 km/h at 2 locations |
| Sale–Bairnsdale | 5.9 | +0.1 | None |

The Traralgon–Sale section continues to show improvement following the drainage remediation works completed in April. However, two locations (TK-047 and TK-052) remain under temporary speed restrictions due to subgrade softening. Julie advised that the permanent repair of these locations is scheduled for late June as part of the maintenance shutdown.

The committee noted that the overall track quality on the line has improved by 8% compared with the same period last year, based on the TQI aggregated across all sections.

**4.2 Signalling & Communications**

Alison Wright tabled the signalling fault summary for April and early May. There were 14 signal-related incidents in April, down from 22 in March. The recurring issue at Moe was again the most significant contributor, with 6 incidents. The fault history report requested at the last meeting has been received by the subcommittee and will be presented at the next meeting. Alison advised that the signalling maintenance provider has identified a faulty relay module at Moe and has ordered a replacement. The module is expected to be installed by 7 June.

**4.3 Level Crossings**

The Level Crossing Upgrade Program is progressing. Works at the Thompsons Road crossing (Moe) are complete, and the crossing was reopened to road traffic on 20 May. The next planned upgrade is at Jacksons Track (Garfield), with works scheduled to commence on 10 June. Tom Berwick noted that the Regional Fast Rail Project has coordinated its possession schedule with the level crossing works to minimise simultaneous disruptions.
